value.content: {"id": "intel_secbyte_interview_architecture", "topic": "sqli", "title": "SecByte Architectural Core: Prepared Statements, Stored Procedures & ORM Security", "source_url": "https://learn.secbyte.org/blog/as2ilat-sql-muqabalat-shughl", "prerequisites": ["rdbms_architecture", "orm_internals"], "signals": ["prepared_statement_binding", "dynamic_stored_procedure", "orm_raw_query", "order_by_clause"], "verification_strategy": "Assess architectural implementation: Verify if ORM uses parameter binding or exposes raw query methods (e.g. Django .extra() or raw SQL). Check if dynamic ORDER BY clauses are validated against a strict property allowlist, as ORDER BY cannot be parameterized using standard prepared statement placeholders.", "evidence_requirements": ["dynamic_order_by_divergence", "orm_raw_fragment_exception"], "remediation": "Validate dynamic sorting/ordering parameters against a strict whitelist of known column names. Use parameterized prepared statements for all filter values. Avoid dynamic SQL concatenation inside stored procedures.", "description": "Comprehensive engineering analysis of SQL mechanics: Stored procedures do NOT inherently prevent SQL injection if dynamic SQL (e.g. EXECUTE IMMEDIATE or sp_executesql) is concatenated inside them. Prepared statements compile the query AST first and treat user inputs strictly as literal values. Critical architectural limitation: Prepared statements cannot parameterize table names or column identifiers in ORDER BY clauses, requiring strict allowlist validation."}
